title: 555 monostable — press once, LED on for a set time

steps.title: The chip
steps.circuit: Start with the chip. Draw the 555 as a box and write each pin number where its wire will meet it. Those numbers are what you convert later.

steps.title: Supply rails and supply pins
steps.circuit: Draw +5 V along the top and 0 V along the bottom. Pins 8 and 4 (Reset) go to +5 V and pin 1 goes to 0 V. Pin 5 is left open.

steps.title: The timing parts: R2 and C1
steps.circuit: R2 runs from +5 V to pin 7. Pin 6 joins pin 7. C1 runs from there to 0 V, + side up. T ≈ 1.1 R2 C1 = 11 s.

steps.title: The trigger: R1 and the slide switch
steps.circuit: SW1's middle pin (common) is on pin 2; its outer pins go to +5 V and 0 V. Slid one way, pin 2 is held at +5 V. Slid the other way, pin 2 goes to 0 V and the pulse starts. Slide it back straight away: while pin 2 is held LOW the output stays HIGH. R1 keeps pin 2 HIGH while the switch is between its two positions.

steps.title: The LED
steps.circuit: From pin 3, R3 and the LED go down to 0 V. The LED is on while pin 3 is HIGH.

steps.title: Test points
steps.circuit: T1 +5 V, T2 0 V, T3 the trigger (pin 2), T4 the output (pin 3).

question.title: 555 monostable — press once, LED on for a set time

seq.title: Place the chip
seq.lead: Start with the chip. Push the 555 across the centre gap with the notch on the left, so pin 1 is bottom left. Now every pin has a column of its own.
seq.how: Then work round the chip: its supply pins first, then the rest one pin at a time. Each pin's net goes in the column that pin is already in.

prompts.text: Where is pin 1? Tap it on the board.

items: 0 V supply lead: − rail along the top, at the top-left corner beside the other supply lead, so both can share one spiral wrap to the power supply.
A black link joins − rail along the top to − rail along the bottom. Both are net 2.
A black link joins column 10 (holes f–j) to − rail along the bottom. Both are net 2.
seq.title: Pin 1: Ground (0 V) → net 2
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 1 joins 0 V, C1, LED1 and SW1. Number it: net 2. Net 2 is the 0 V supply.
seq.how: Pin 1 is in column 10 (holes f–j), so that column is net 2.

items: +5 V supply lead: + rail along the top, at the top-left corner beside the other supply lead, so both can share one spiral wrap to the power supply.
A red link joins + rail along the top to + rail along the bottom. Both are net 1.
A red link joins + rail along the top to column 10 (holes a–e). Both are net 1.
A red link joins column 13 (holes f–j) to + rail along the bottom. Both are net 1.
seq.title: Pin 4: Reset → net 1
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 4 joins +5 V, R1, R2 and SW1. Number it: net 1. Net 1 is the +5 V supply.
seq.how: Pin 4 is in column 13 (holes f–j), so that column is net 1. Pin 8 is on net 1 too, so its column joins in.

items: R1 goes in now, from net 3 (column 11, holes f–j) to net 1 (column 14, holes f–j).
SW1 goes in now. Its 3 legs go in net 1 (column 6, holes f–j), net 3 (column 7, holes f–j) and net 2 (column 8, holes f–j), in that order.
A red link joins column 14 (holes f–j) to + rail along the bottom. Both are net 1.
A red link joins column 6 (holes f–j) to + rail along the bottom. Both are net 1.
A green link joins column 7 (holes f–j) to column 11 (holes f–j). Both are net 3.
A black link joins column 8 (holes f–j) to − rail along the bottom. Both are net 2.

prompts.text: R1 joins net 3 to net 1. Tap where its other leg goes.

seq.title: Pin 2: Trigger → net 3
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 2 joins SW1 and R1. Number it: net 3.
seq.how: Pin 2 is in column 11 (holes f–j), so that column is net 3.

seq.title: Pin 3: Output → net 5
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 3 joins R3. Number it: net 5.
seq.how: Pin 3 is in column 12 (holes f–j), so that column is net 5.

items: R2 goes in now, from net 1 (+ rail along the top) to net 4 (column 11, holes a–e).
C1 goes in now, from net 4 (column 12, holes a–e) to net 2 (− rail along the top).
A yellow link joins column 11 (holes a–e) to column 12 (holes a–e). Both are net 4.

prompts.text: R2 joins net 4 to net 1. Tap where its other leg goes.

seq.title: Pin 6: Threshold → net 4
seq.lead: On the diagram, pin 6 joins R2 and C1. Number it: net 4.
seq.how: Pin 6 is in column 12 (holes a–e), so that column is net 4. Pin 7 is on net 4 too, so its column joins in.

items: R3 goes in now, from net 5 (column 12, holes f–j) to net 6 (column 15, holes f–j).
LED1 goes in now, from net 6 (column 15, holes f–j) to net 2 (column 16, holes f–j).
A black link joins column 16 (holes f–j) to − rail along the bottom. Both are net 2.

prompts.text: R3 joins net 6 to net 5. Tap where its other leg goes.

seq.title: Net 6: R3 and LED1
seq.lead: R3 and LED1 meet away from the chip. Number it: net 6.
seq.how: Give net 6 a free column: column 15 (holes f–j).

seq.title: Test points
seq.lead: Mark a test point on each net you will measure, before you build.
seq.how: T1 on net 1, T2 on net 2, T3 on net 3, T4 on net 5.

seq.title: Check it against the diagram
seq.lead: Read the board back one column at a time and compare it with the numbered nets.
seq.how: Every net must be one column, or columns joined by a link, and no two nets may touch.

mistakes.title: Board A
mistakes.why: Right. C1's + leg is in the 0 V rail and its − leg is in the timing column. An electrolytic capacitor's + leg goes on the more positive net, here net 4.

options.t: C1 is the wrong way round
R2 is in the wrong column
options.fb: R2 runs from the + rail to pin 7's column, as the diagram shows. Look at the parts that only work one way round.

options.t: The chip is not across the centre gap
options.fb: The 555 sits across the gap, so its two rows are kept apart. Check which leg of C1 is in the 0 V rail.

options.t: The LED is the wrong way round
options.fb: The LED's long leg is in R3's column, which is right. Look for the other part that only works one way round.

mistakes.title: Board B
mistakes.why: Right. The red link from pin 4's column to the + rail is missing. Pin 4 is Reset. Joined to nothing, it can stop the timer working. Pin 4 must be on net 1, +5 V.

options.t: Pin 4 has no link to +5 V
C1 is the wrong way round
options.fb: C1's + leg is in the timing column, which is right. Check every chip pin that should go to a rail.

options.t: R3 has both legs in one column
options.fb: R3 runs from pin 3's column to the LED's column, so it isn't shorted. Follow pins 8 and 4 to the + rail.

options.t: Pin 1 has no link to 0 V
options.fb: The black link from pin 1's column to the 0 V rail is there. Check the other supply pins.

mistakes.title: Board C
mistakes.why: Right. Both of R3's legs are in column 12, so R3 is shorted out. Nothing joins pin 3 to the LED's column, so the LED never lights.

options.t: R3 has both legs in one column, so it is shorted out
The LED is the wrong way round
options.fb: The LED's long leg is in the column R3 should reach. Look at how R3 is fitted.

options.t: R3 should be a link wire
options.fb: R3 limits the LED current, so it must stay a resistor. Look at which columns its two legs are in.

options.t: The chip is in the wrong place
options.fb: The 555 sits across the centre gap, as it should. Follow R3's two legs.

quiz.q: The monostable diagram has 6 numbered nets. What is the fewest number of columns and rails the breadboard can use?
o: Right. Each net needs its own column or rail, so 6 is the fewest. A net can spread over more than one column if a link joins them.
Each net needs a column or rail of its own, or two nets would be joined. Count the numbers on the diagram.
8, one per chip pin
Some pins share a net (pins 6 and 7 do), so they can share a column. Count the nets, not the pins.
That would leave columns unused. Each net needs at least one column or rail: count the numbers.

quiz.q: Why does the 555 sit across the centre gap?
o: So the pins opposite each other are not joined
Right. Each column is joined top to bottom on its own side of the gap. Across the gap, pin 1 and pin 8 are in separate columns.
To stop the chip overheating
The gap is about which pins are connected, not heat. Which pins would share a column without it?
So the chip fits the power rails
The rails run along the edges, away from the chip. Think about pin 1 and pin 8 in the same column.
It doesn't matter where the chip goes
On one side of the gap, pins opposite each other would share a column. Think about pin 1 and pin 8.

quiz.q: Two legs are labelled with net 4 on the diagram. Where must they go on the breadboard?
o: In the same column, or columns joined by a link
Right. Same number means connected.
In columns next to each other
Next-door columns are not connected. Same number means the same column, or a link.
Anywhere, as long as there is a test point
A test point measures a net; it doesn't join one. Same number means connected.
In different columns, so they don't short
That is the rule for different numbers. The same number must be joined.
